essence: Find the need behind a bad habit, then reframe what you want.
modern_lens: Chapter 10 says every craving is a surface version of a deeper motive such as connection, status, relief or certainty. Bad habits are usually a costly answer to a real need. Naming the need lets you find a better answer, and reframing a good habit can make it feel like an opportunity rather than a chore.

ideas.name: Deeper Motives Behind Cravings
ideas.text: You do not really crave scrolling; you crave connection, novelty or relief from boredom. Each habit is a modern answer to an old need such as belonging, approval, certainty or saving energy. Once you know the need, you can choose a better answer.
ideas.try: For one bad habit, finish the sentence: what I really want in that moment is…

ideas.name: Predictions Become Feelings
ideas.text: Cravings arise when the brain predicts that a change of state would feel better. The same cue can produce different feelings depending on how you interpret it. Change the prediction and the craving changes too.
ideas.try: Next time a craving hits, write what you predict will happen, then what actually happens.

ideas.name: Get To, Not Have To
ideas.text: Small changes in wording change how a habit feels. 'I have to go to the gym' becomes 'I get to build strength'. 'I have to present' becomes 'I get to show my team's work'. The behaviour is the same; the meaning is more attractive.
ideas.try: Rewrite three of today's 'have to' tasks as 'get to' sentences.

ideas.name: Build a Motivation Ritual
ideas.text: Pair something you enjoy with a short routine, then do that routine before a hard task. Over time the routine itself triggers a good mood and focus. A three-song playlist before writing or a short walk before calls can work.
ideas.try: Choose a two-minute warm-up ritual and do it before your hardest task for one week.

ideas.name: Spell Out the Costs
ideas.text: To make a bad habit unattractive, highlight what it really costs: hours, money, health, relationships. A vivid list of costs, kept where you will see it, changes the prediction your brain makes when the cue appears.
ideas.try: Calculate the yearly cost of one bad habit in money or hours and post the number where you will see it.
